Team — forwarding EmberTech numbers (below). Can you run a two-variant sizing sims and return a short slate by 3pm PT?

Two modeling asks:
1) Primary model: rw-13B-fp16 (recommended for quality). Provide tokens/sec per N GPU slab, expected p95 latency at 1k / 2.5k / 5k token/sec inputs, and GPUs required to meet 95th <=180ms.
2) Fallback model: rw-13B-quant8 (lower perf, higher throughput). Provide same table plus guidance on when to route to fallback (latency/cost thresholds).

Constraints / preferences from customer:
- Target 95th latency <= 180ms, soft cap 300ms
- Commit model: monthly slab(s) with ability to burst to extra slabs for campaign windows (DocuSign preferred for faster execution)
- Headroom target: prefer 1.8x sustained peak, and an extra burst buffer for 30–60m spikes

Deliverable: consolidated table (GPU count / tokens/sec / estimated monthly cost / predicted p95 latency) + recommended commit (slab sizes and burst plan). Attach the throughput_simulation_v1.pdf to the reply.

Thanks — Jordan

Quick pass — attaching throughput_simulation_v1.pdf with calculations. Summary here:

Assumptions
- Primary model: rw-13B-fp16 -> baseline throughput we measured on p4d-like slab = ~1,300 tokens/sec per GPU for 300-token sequences (numbers downscale for longer sequences).
- Quantized variant: rw-13B-quant8 -> ~2,400 tokens/sec per GPU (lower mem and faster kernels).
- Network and KV cache overhead: plan +10% on top of raw tokens/sec.

Sizing table (rounded):
- Target sustained day: 1,100 tps -> Primary: 1 GPU (1,300 tps) fits but no headroom. With 1.8x headroom => 2 GPUs; with burst buffer (x2 short-term) => recommend commit 3 GPUs + 1 burst slab.
- Target peak window: 5,200 tps -> Primary: 5,200 / 1,300 = ~4.0 GPUs raw -> with 1.8x headroom => ~8 GPUs. Quantized gives: 5,200 / 2,400 = ~2.2 -> with 1.8x => ~4 GPUs.

Recommendation
- Commit: 4 primary GPUs (rw-13B-fp16) as committed slab for steady+headroom; provide 4 additional burst GPUs available via reserved spare pool for campaign windows (gives 2x peak capacity).
- Fallback route: use rw-13B-quant8 on 2 slabs for heavy burst traffic if latency permits. That reduces committed cost by ~30% but increases regression risk; include a canary rollout for 2 weeks.
- Expected p95 latency: with 4 primary GPUs at 5,200 tps we estimate ~230ms (miss target). With 8 primary GPUs -> ~130ms (meets 180ms). Quantized 4 GPUs -> ~150ms but with lower quality.

Next steps
- Karthik: can you produce an SLO-fit chart (p95 latency vs tokens/sec) for both variants and a cost delta table?
- Jordan: loop in procurement and attach a sample DocuSign SKU for 4 + 4 burst slabs so procurement has an anchor.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alicia / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick data. Ben ran a modeling pass and attached a short PDF with the math. High-level proposal for EmberTech:

- Commit: 4 primary GPUs (rw-13B-fp16) as the baseline slab to cover steady usage + minimal headroom.
- Burst: add 4 burst GPUs (on-demand reserved pool) for campaign windows. This gives ~2x available peak capacity and meets the customer headroom ask.
- Fallback plan: 2 quantized slabs (rw-13B-quant8) for short bursts where slight quality drop is acceptable.

If procurement is comfortable, I can have a draft contract + DocuSign with those SKUs and monthly cost estimates ready by EOD tomorrow. DocuSign preview: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/preview/EMB-20270520-contract (placeholder).

Proposed operational guardrails:
- Autoscale buffer threshold at 70% of committed tokens/sec to trigger warm-up of burst slabs.
- Canary: route 5% of traffic to quantized model for 7 days before expanding.

Alicia — would a commit of 4+4 slabs align with your procurement constraints? If yes, we’ll push a formal quote and DD materials (SOC2 evidence pack) to Procurement.

Thanks — Jordan
